name: Sharpen scissors
blurb: Scissors are two blades that shear past each other, so sharpening them means restoring the bevel without touching the flat inner faces. Easy once you know that rule.
gear: A whetstone or a fine file
A screwdriver if the pivot is adjustable
steps: Check the pivot first: many “blunt” scissors are simply loose. Tighten until the blades shear with slight resistance.
Separate the blades if the design allows, or work them open.
Sharpen only the outer bevel, matching its existing angle, with strokes running from pivot to tip.
Never grind the flat inner faces — that is the shearing surface and ruins the scissors.
Remove the burr by opening and closing the scissors a few times, or with a light pass on a strop.
Oil the pivot and test on tissue paper, which exposes any gap along the cut.
tips: Cutting tissue paper cleanly to the tip is the real test; thick paper hides a lot of faults.
Fabric scissors should never cut paper. Keep two pairs and label them.
proof: Your blunt kitchen scissors cut tissue paper cleanly along the full length of the blade.
